mainTopic: תֶּמֶד (watery grape-residue drink): when it counts as real produce, for buying with כסף מעשר שני and for tithing
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining that the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים about תמד is only once it has fermented, and that our משנה follows רבי יהודה. רב נחמן then quotes רבה בר אבוה: if תמד was bought with כסף מעשר and later fermented, the purchase works, because it turns out it was produce all along. The גמרא challenges this from the משנה, which flatly says unfermented תמד cannot be bought, even though it might have fermented later. רבה answers that the משנה means a case where a sample kept in a cup never fermented. רבא answers differently: the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who in a משנה about a מקוה judges a liquid by how it looks right now, and unfermented תמד looks and tastes like water. The גמרא then notes that רבי אלעזר disagrees with רב נחמן. He holds the argument is about unfermented תמד, and even רבי יהודה only requires tithing it from itself, so that one will not tithe between obligated and exempt produce. Finally, a new ברייתא about תמד before it ferments begins, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The dispute is only once the תמד has fermented
steps.stepSummary: The argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים about תמד applies only after it fermented, and our משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the תמד fermented, there is a dispute, and our משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an earlier discussion. It explains that the argument about תמד is only about תמד that has already fermented. It also says our משנה follows רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before fermenting, everyone agrees תמד is just water. After it ferments and tastes like wine, רבי יהודה treats it like wine and the חכמים do not. Our משנה treats fermented תמד like wine, so it must follow רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: A weak drink made by pouring water over leftover grape skins and seeds after pressing
It fermented (it turned sour and wine-like)
A dispute between Sages
Our משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Here הֶחְמִיץ does not mean it turned into vinegar. It means the תמד fermented and became like wine.

phrases.english: When it fermented, there is a dispute,
phrases.notes: "It" is the תמד, the watery drink made from grape leftovers that the גמרא was already discussing.

phrases.english: and our Mishnah follows Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Wraps up the earlier discussion about where the dispute over תמד lies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute over תמד is only once it fermented; our משנה follows רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Another Sage says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא also says the dispute is only when the תמד fermented.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too, רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא said: when it fermented, there is a dispute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another Sage who says exactly the same thing. This backs up the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new idea is added here. The point is that a second authority holds the same view, which makes it stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: And likewise (another source says the same)

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: And likewise Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, said:
When it fermented, there is a dispute.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 1 with a matching statement from another Sage.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the dispute applies only to fermented תמד
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רבי יוסי ברבי חנינא

steps.title: תמד that fermented after it was bought counts as a good purchase
steps.stepSummary: If someone bought unfermented תמד with כסף מעשר and it later fermented, the purchase works, because it turns out it was produce from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: תמד that was bought with מעשר money and later fermented becomes מעשר. Why? Because it turns out, looking back, that it was produce all along.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching begins. If you bought unfermented תמד with כסף מעשר שני and it fermented later, the purchase counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You may only spend כסף מעשר שני on food or drink, not on plain water. When the תמד ferments later, this shows it was really a grape product from the start (למפרע). So the purchase was valid all along.

keyTerms.meaning: Money that holds the holiness of מעשר שני and may only be spent on food or drink
The item bought takes on the holiness of מעשר
The matter became revealed (it turned out)
Looking back, from the beginning
Produce, a real food item

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a later event can show what something was all along (איגלאי מילתא למפרע) comes up all over ש"ס.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: And Rav Naḥman said that Rabba bar Avuh said:
Temed that one bought with tithe money,
phrases.notes: This is money of מעשר שני, which may only be spent on food and drink.

phrases.english: and in the end it fermented: it acquired tithe status.
What is the reason?
The matter was revealed retroactively
that it was produce.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching about buying תמד with כסף מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unfermented תמד bought with כסף מעשר that later ferments is a valid purchase, because it turns out it was produce from the start.

steps.title: Challenge: maybe the unfermented תמד would have fermented later
steps.stepSummary: If fermenting later makes the purchase valid, how can the משנה say flatly that unfermented תמד cannot be bought? Maybe it would have fermented if left alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then our משנה, which teaches that if it fermented, yes, and if it did not ferment, no — maybe if he had left it, it would have fermented!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבה בר אבוה's rule using the משנה. The משנה says unfermented תמד may not be bought with כסף מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By רבה בר אבוה's logic, what the תמד does later decides its status. So how can the משנה rule against unfermented תמד right away? It might still ferment and turn out to have been produce.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
He left it alone
Yes / no

phrases.english: But then the Mishnah that teaches:
If it fermented, yes; if it did not ferment, no,
phrases.notes: "Yes" means you may buy it with מעשר money; "no" means you may not.

phrases.english: perhaps if he had left it, it would have fermented!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, מַתְנִיתִין דְּקָתָנֵי הֶחְמִיץ – אִין, לֹא הֶחְמִיץ – לָא
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule of רבה בר אבוה that later fermentation shows the תמד was produce all along
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If later fermentation decides the status, the משנה cannot flatly rule against unfermented תמד, since it might still ferment.

steps.title: רבה: the משנה means some was kept in a cup and never fermented
steps.stepSummary: רבה explains that the משנה is talking about a case where some of the תמד was saved in a cup and it never fermented.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: the case is where he left some of it in a cup and it did not ferment.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers the challenge. In the משנה, some of the תמד was kept aside in a cup, and it never fermented.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the saved sample never fermented, we know for sure the תמד was never produce. So the purchase fails. This fits with רבה בר אבוה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He left over, kept some aside
A cup

phrases.english: Rabba said:
When he left some of it in a cup and it did not ferment.
phrases.notes: The saved cup is a test sample. It shows what the rest of the תמד would have done.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to rule on unfermented תמד even though it might still ferment.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a case where a saved sample proved the תמד never fermented.

steps.title: רבא: the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a different answer: the משנה follows the view of רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: whose view is this משנה? It is רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the same challenge in a different way. He says the משנה follows one specific תנא, רבי יוחנן בן נורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא does not need רבה's cup case. He says the משנה follows a Sage with his own approach, which the גמרא is about to show. This way the משנה does not have to fit רבה בר אבוה's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?

phrases.english: Rava said: Whose view is this?
It is Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: הָא מַנִּי? רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A different answer to the challenge of step 4, instead of רבה's.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must fit רבה בר אבוה's rule, which forced רבה to limit it to the cup case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, so it need not be limited to that case.

steps.title: The משנה in מקואות about wine-colored water
steps.stepSummary: רבא quotes a משנה: almost three לוגין of water plus a little wine, which looks like wine, falls into a מקוה and does not make it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: three לוגין of water missing a קורטוב, into which a קורטוב of wine fell, and they look like wine, and they fell into a מקוה — they did not make it פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings his source for רבי יוחנן בן נורי's view, a משנה about a מקוה. The גמרא sets this up here and explains how it connects in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three לוגין of drawn water makes a מקוה פסול. Here there was less than three לוגין of water, plus a little wine that made the mixture look like wine. In this wine case the מקוה stays kosher on every view. The real argument shows up in the milk case in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: Plural of לוֹג, a liquid measure
A tiny measure (1/64 of a לוֹג)
A ritual bath
They made it invalid (פסול)

steps.confusionAlert: There is less than three לוגין of water here. The extra קורטוב that brings it up to three לוגין is wine, not water.

phrases.english: As we learned in a Mishnah:
Three log of water less a kortov,
phrases.notes: Three לוגין of drawn water is the amount that makes a מקוה פסול, so having just under that amount matters.

phrases.english: into which a kortov of wine fell,
and their appearance is like the appearance of wine,
and they fell into a ritual bath: they did not invalidate it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: שְׁלֹשָׁה לוּגִּין מַיִם חָסֵר קוּרְטוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for רבא's claim in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that our משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה מקואות about almost three לוגין of water mixed with a קורטוב of wine

steps.title: The milk case in the מקוה משנה
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues: almost three לוגין of water, completed by a little milk and still looking like water, falls into a מקוה and does not make it פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are three לוגין of water minus a tiny amount, and that tiny amount of milk fell in, and it all still looks like water, and it fell into a מקוה, it does not make the מקוה פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the same משנה from step 7, now giving a second case with milk instead of wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three לוגין of drawn water make a מקוה פסול. Here the actual water is just under three לוגין, and the milk only fills the gap. The תנא קמא says the milk does not count as water, even though the mixture looks like water.

keyTerms.meaning: Milk

phrases.english: Three לוגין of water less one קורטוב,
phrases.notes: This is drawn water, the kind that can make a מקוה פסול when there are three full לוגין.

phrases.english: into which a קורטוב of milk fell,
and their appearance is like the appearance of water,
and they fell into a מקוה: they did not make it פסול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same משנה quoted in step 7 with a parallel case using milk.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's claim that our משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מקואות about three לוגין of drawn water

steps.title: רבי יוחנן בן נורי: everything follows the appearance
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן בן נורי disagrees with the תנא קמא and says the status of the liquid depends on how it looks.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן בן נורי says: everything goes according to how it looks.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה brings the opposing opinion, and this is the opinion רבא needs for his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the mixture looks like water, רבי יוחנן בן נורי treats all of it as water. So there are three full לוגין of water, and the מקוה is פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: Everything follows the appearance
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up רבי יוחנן בן נורי, the תנא in this משנה, with the אמורא רבי יוחנן. The next line says 'רבי יוחנן' but means רבי יוחנן בן נורי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan ben Nuri says:
Everything follows the appearance.
phrases.notes: So in the milk case the mixture counts as water, and the מקוה is פסול.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי אוֹמֵר: הַכֹּל הוֹלֵךְ אַחַר הַמַּרְאֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the quoted משנה, which is the view רבא relies on.
steps.raayaObject: Our משנה follows a 'go by appearance' view
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יוחנן בן נורי in משנה מקואות

steps.title: רבא applies the appearance rule to unfermented תמד
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that since רבי יוחנן בן נורי goes by appearance, unfermented תמד, which tastes and looks like water, is water. So it cannot be bought with כסף מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doesn't רבי יוחנן בן נורי say we go by how it looks? Here too, go by how it looks, and the taste and look of this liquid are water.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא connects the quoted משנה to our case and finishes his answer to the קשיא from step 4.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יוחנן בן נורי, we judge the liquid by what it is like now, not by what it may become later. Unfermented תמד is water right now, so the משנה rules flatly that it cannot be bought. רב נחמן's rule in step 3 follows the תנא קמא, who does not go by appearance.

keyTerms.meaning: We go after the appearance
Taste

steps.whatToRemember: רבא: our משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who judges a liquid by how it looks now. Unfermented תמד looks and tastes like water, so it cannot be bought with כסף מעשר, even if it ferments later.

phrases.english: Doesn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
phrases.notes: This means רבי יוחנן בן נורי from the משנה just quoted.

phrases.english: we go after the appearance?
Here too, go after the appearance,
phrases.notes: 'Here' is our משנה about buying תמד with כסף מעשר.

phrases.english: and the taste and appearance of this are water.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאו אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בָּתַר חֲזוּתָא אָזְלִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies רבי יוחנן בן נורי's rule from step 9 to explain our משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the משנה to a specific תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If later fermenting can make the purchase work, the משנה should not rule flatly that unfermented תמד cannot be bought.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן נורי, who judges by present appearance, so unfermented תמד counts as water.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר disagrees with רב נחמן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב נחמן's view disagrees with רבי אלעזר, who says everyone agrees you may not separate מעשר for this תמד from תמד somewhere else unless it fermented.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי אלעזר, because רבי אלעזר said: everyone agrees that we do not separate מעשר for it from a different place unless it fermented.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the חכמים about tithing תמד. It points out that רבי אלעזר sees that מחלוקת differently than רב נחמן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן said that if the תמד has not fermented, even רבי יהודה agrees there is no obligation to tithe it. רבי אלעזר implies that, according to רבי יהודה, the obligation already exists before fermenting, and the only thing everyone agrees on is that you cannot tithe it from תמד somewhere else. So the two disagree about unfermented תמד.

keyTerms.meaning: And it disagrees
Everyone agrees
Separate (מעשר or תרומה)
From a different place, meaning from other produce

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows there are two ways to understand the רבי יהודה and חכמים מחלוקת: does it apply only after the תמד ferments, or before as well?

phrases.english: And it disagrees with Rabbi Elazar,
phrases.notes: 'It' is רב נחמן's earlier statement that the מחלוקת between רבי יהודה and the חכמים is only about fermented תמד.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Elazar said:
Everyone agrees that one may not separate for it

phrases.aramaic: מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הֶחְמִיץ.
phrases.english: from another place, unless it fermented.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבא's answer and returns to רב נחמן's statement in step 1 that the dispute is only about fermented תמד, noting that רבי אלעזר disagrees with it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: everyone agrees that unfermented תמד may not be tithed from תמד in another place, only after it ferments.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר places the argument on unfermented תמד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי אלעזר holds the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים is about תמד that has not fermented.
steps.simpleTranslation: He holds that the argument is about תמד that did not ferment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining what רבי אלעזר is thinking. It tells us which case he thinks the famous argument is about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 11, רבי אלעזר said everyone agrees you cannot tithe this תמד from other תמד unless it fermented. To understand that, the גמרא first sets his starting point: the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים is about unfermented תמד. The next step builds on this.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds, meaning this is his opinion

phrases.english: He holds that the argument is where it did not ferment,
phrases.notes: "He" is רבי אלעזר, and the argument is the one between רבי יהודה and the חכמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind רבי אלעזר's statement in Step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אלעזר, the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים is about unfermented תמד.

steps.title: רבי יהודה requires tithing only from the same תמד
steps.stepSummary: Even רבי יהודה only requires tithing unfermented תמד from that same batch, not from other תמד, because of the fear of mixing obligated and exempt produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה only obligates tithing from that same תמד itself. But you may not tithe it from תמד somewhere else, because you might end up separating from obligated produce for exempt produce, or from exempt produce for obligated produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining רבי אלעזר. Even רבי יהודה, the strict opinion, only allows tithing the תמד from itself, and gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unfermented תמד may or may not have the status of wine, so it may or may not need מעשר. If you tithe from other תמד, one batch might be obligated and the other exempt. Separating מעשר between an obligated batch and an exempt batch does not work, so it is not allowed. That is why everyone, even רבי יהודה, agrees you cannot use תמד from elsewhere.

keyTerms.meaning: It only goes this far, meaning he only said it in this case
From it and in it, meaning from the same batch
From elsewhere, from a different batch
To separate, meaning to set aside מעשר
Produce that is obligated in מעשר
Produce that is exempt from מעשר

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי אלעזר, רבי יהודה requires tithing unfermented תמד, but only from itself. Tithing it from other תמד risks mixing obligated and exempt produce. The חכמים do not require tithing it at all.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though רבי יהודה is the one who obligates tithing, he does not allow tithing from just any תמד. He only allows it from the same batch.

phrases.aramaic: וְעַד כָּאן לָא מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: And רבי יהודה only obligates
from it and in it itself,
but from elsewhere, no,
perhaps he will come to separate
from the obligated for the exempt
and from the exempt for the obligated.
phrases.notes: Obligated means fermented תמד, which counts as wine. Exempt means תמד that never ferments.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעַד כָּאן לָא מְחַיֵּיב רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אֶלָּא מִינֵּיהּ וּבֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation from Step 12 and shows why רבי אלעזר says everyone agrees about tithing from elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even רבי יהודה only requires tithing unfermented תמד from itself, not from other תמד, so that you will not separate between obligated and exempt produce.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains how רבי אלעזר can say 'everyone agrees' even though רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue. It also shows why this view does not fit רב נחמן's view.

steps.title: A new ברייתא about תמד before it ferments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא about תמד before it ferments. The ruling continues in the next section.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: תמד, before it has fermented —
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is opening a new ברייתא. This line is only the setup, and the actual law comes in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic stays the same: the status of תמד before fermenting. But now the source is a ברייתא, not the opinions of the אמוראים. The ברייתא will tell us how unfermented תמד is treated.

keyTerms.meaning: Before, literally 'until it has not yet'
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
תמד, before it has fermented —
